| [NOTE-364](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-364.md) | The Self as a Center of Narrative Gravity | A self is an abstractum like a centre of gravity, posited by interpretation, and like a fictional character it is indeterminate beyond what its story fixes. A mindless novel-writing robot can author a self whose story is true of the robot. Brains are bundles of partly autonomous systems that make themselves cohere into one autobiography, and when the story coheres around two points there are two selves. | [NOTE-377](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-377.md) | Philosophical conceptions of the self: implications for cognitive science | A short review that sets the minimal self (present self-consciousness) against the narrative self (extended in time), splits the minimal self into a sense of ownership and a sense of agency, and ties their dissociation in schizophrenic thought insertion to Frith's forward comparator model. Evidence is cited, not shown. | Read |
| [NOTE-383](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-383.md) | Against Narrativity | Rejects the descriptive and the normative Narrativity theses. Separates Diachronic from Episodic self-experience, and form-finding, story-telling and revision within Narrativity. Places Dennett, Schechtman, Sartre and himself on that grid. | [NOTE-470](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-470.md) | “First we invented stories, then they changed us”: The Evolution of Narrative Identity | McAdams's review essay on narrative identity: "the internalized and evolving story a person invents to explain how he or she has become the person he or she is becoming".
